It sounds like you've been putting real effort into this relationship—trying to coordinate plans, communicate openly, and even honestly reflecting on whether her criticisms hold truth. That kind of self-awareness is a strength, not a flaw, and it's the opposite of being "oblivious" or "self-consumed."

Here's something worth noticing: you've never heard these labels from anyone else. That's important information. Her frustration when plans don't go her way seems to be more about her temperament than an accurate mirror of who you are. You can hold compassion for where she's coming from while still refusing to accept a distorted picture of yourself.

You don't have to keep absorbing comments that leave you hurt. It's okay to set a gentle limit—"I want to enjoy your visit, but I won't continue conversations that turn into criticisms of my character." Protecting your peace isn't inconsiderate; it's healthy. If the hurt lingers, talking it through with a trusted friend or counselor can help you sort truth from someone else's frustration.
